I'm checking three candidate objections against the R&D-internalization question: B1 says the GDP-price link is confounded by omitted variables and reflects willingness to pay for current health, A10 says the log contribution is just mechanical scaling with GDP, and A7 says an elasticity above one mixes general health spending with strategic under-contribution. I'm now noting that B1 overlaps with A7 because both treat willingness to pay for health as the thing being measured.

I'm weighing whether A7 and B1 target the same concern, since both treat willingness to pay for health as what the GDP relation is picking up, and I'd put that match at around 55 percent. A10 looks like a different problem, since it is about mechanical scaling with GDP rather than confounding by omitted variables. I'm also noting that A12 only addresses the GDP correlation in general, so it matches B1 as the same topic but not the same concern. B2 has no real counterpart, so I'll set it aside, and the same study looks like the right match here: pharma pricing, GDP, and R&D from Frech et al.
